Commentary.Commentary: That's was some lively entertaining passage of play in this game. Afghanistan lost their last 6 wickets in space of 60 runs. However, they have a lead of 113 runs. Not  a big lead but could be a tricky time for Zimbabwe batters who are already tired after being on the field for more than three days. It's a rarity that we see a double centurion but Afghanistan had a couple of them. Rahmat Shah and Hashmatullah Shahidi have been brilliant. Afsar Zazai notched a ton as well. Brian Bennett was the pick of the lot as he took a five fer. Afghanistan now will hope they can quickly take some wickets and try and get a result out of this match. Stay tuned.

The rainy Day 4 has left no option for a result but a draw looks like the only possible result we could foresee. Afghanistan trail by 71 runs and the first thing they'll try is to cut the deficit and try and take the lead. We could see some aggressive cricket from Afghanistan if they push for a win here but that looks more than impossible. Zimbabwe on the other hand have been grinding hard for wickets and have to do the same today. It's overcast conditions today as well at Queens Sports Club, Bulawayo. Let's hope the rain stays away and we get a lot of action. Stay tuned.
...DAY 5, SESSION 1...

The deficit is only 71 now but the problem now is time! Just the one day left! Day 5 can either be extremely entertaining or could be just like the last 4 days. We expect Afghanistan to play some attacking brand of cricket but first, we hope for the rain gods to stay away. Do join us for the action, play begins an hour before. Until then, goodbye and take care!

THE INEVITABLE HAS HAPPENED! Play has been CALLED OFF! Just the one session of play was possible. The players did walk out after Lunch, there were a few balls bowled but then it started raining and it just did not stop. In the one session played earlier, it was Afghanistan who dominated it. They lost Shah early but Shahidi and Zazai put up another good stand.
The covers are firmly in place! The rain seems to have eased out and there's a supersopper doing rounds but the outfield seems to have taken a real beating and will take time to dry.

A flawless day with the bat for the visitors sees them in the ascendancy! The duo of Shah and Shahidi have amassed over 300 between them and got the deficit down to just the 161 runs. Zimbabwe are tired, in their minds and their legs too but they have to grind harder to get the breakthrough. Let's hope we get some equal entertainment on Day 4. Commentary.Commentary: All set for action. The players are out in the middle. Shahidi and Shah to resume their innings. Shah is on 49. Here is Blessing Muzarabani with just a slip on offer.

Afghanistan have a long batting line up but it's the partnership between Shahidi and Shah could be pivotal in this game. If they bat for a long period, Afghanistan could at least get close to Zimbabwe's score but that is still very far. Zimbabwe need to make early inroads and there could be enough help for them with overcast conditions. Rain is expected throughout the day but let's hope we get an interrupted action. Stay tuned.

The partnership between Hashmatullah Shahidi and Rahmat Shah has held this game in fine balance so far. Still, Zimbabwe's 586 means they are still well on top but the way the pitch is playing, we expect Day 3 to move quickly. We saw in the last session of Day 2, the pitch started to deteriorate and it could just help the Zimbabwe bowlers a bit.
...DAY 3, SESSION 1...

Afghanistan also need a couple of their players to score big. They still trail by a long way but their first aim will be to avoid the follow-on. It is a test for their batters. Zimbabwe on the other hand, just need to hit the right lines and lengths on a pitch which is now offering something for the bowlers and be patient. Day 3 can indicate as to which way this game is heading. Do join us for the coverage at 7.30 am GMT. Till then, goodbye and take care!

With the ball, Zimbabwe got a wicket early courtesy of Gwandu. Shah and Malik then put up a good start but the latter fell after getting off to a start. Shahidi and Shah though have ensured there are no more wickets to fall on Day 2.

The inevitable has happened! It is officially Stumps! The light was never going to improve and we have ran out of time. Nevertheless, it has been another very good day of Test cricket, especially for the hosts. They amassed their highest score and it was Ervine and Bennett who started for them with the bat on Day 2.

Drinks! A good start by Afghanistan. Shah is batting well so far and Shahidi is supporting nicely as well. Zimbabwe are currently working with spinners but are not getting much purchase from the flat. Probably another 5-6 overs to go before stumps as it's very gloomy now.
